verdictBasis: Three blockers survive independent measurement. The artifact's central enforcement-honesty posture is, on my own recount, SOUND: the 2x7x2 decomposition is real and complete, the census replicates cell-for-cell, and each of the four cells carrying an enforced value names a mechanism that exists on both platforms and delivers exactly the confinement it claims and no more. The blockers are not in the enforcement column. Two are measurement/recital defects that do not replicate at bytes (freeze 7.2.2), one of them inside the fixture class the artifact itself nominates as the falsifier of its central claim; the third is an outcome-to-disclosure mapping the artifact left undefined for a record value it created, with its own wording golden mandating a false statement in that case. Each is small to repair and none requires re-deciding the design.

blockers.title: FX-2B recites 'ten of twenty-eight cells' where the artifact's own mechanical census says 24 of 28, and errs in the flattering direction
blockers.quotedAtBytes: This class exists because the honest claim on ten of twenty-eight cells is 'there is no enforcement', and a claim of no-enforcement is falsifiable and must be tested like any other.
blockers.whatIMeasured: I recounted the ENFORCED column mechanically over truthTables.tables: 28 cells total, DISCLOSURE-ONLY 24, ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION 2, ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER 2. That replicates enforcedColumnCensus.byState and byPlatformAndMode exactly. The number 10 is the count of DISCLOSURE-ONLY cells in the child-process mode alone (5 macos + 5 linux); the in-host-process mode adds 14 more (7 + 7). The denominator in the sentence is the full 28, so the sentence states the predicate 'there is no enforcement' as holding on 10 of 28 cells when it holds on 24 of 28.
blockers.internalContradiction: enforcedColumnCensus.readThisWay states, of the same fixture, 'every one of the 24 disclosure-only cells is now NAMED, carries an affirmative disclosure obligation, and has a fixture class (FX-2B)'. The artifact therefore gives FX-2B a 24-cell coverage obligation in one place and a 10-cell one in another.
blockers.whyBlocking: Freeze 7.2.2 gives measurements a hard comparison: a recited count that does not replicate is a defect even when the conclusion survives. This one does not merely fail to replicate, it fails in the direction that understates how many cells have no enforcement, on the single axis the artifact is organized around, inside the class reviewGuidance.whatWouldFalsifyTheCentralClaim names as the falsification mechanism. A reader sizing FX-2B's obligation from its own text would build a fixture set covering 10 cells and leave 14 disclosure-only cells with no negative-space evidence, which is exactly how a DISCLOSURE-ONLY cell silently starts reading as enforced.
blockers.repair: State the count that replicates. Either 'twenty-four of twenty-eight cells' for the whole table, or, if the intent was mode-scoped, 'ten of the fourteen child-process cells (and all fourteen in-host-process cells, per FX-10)'. Whichever is chosen must agree with readThisWay.

blockers.title: The GRANTED column's binding tuple is labelled 'file 03's binding list, carried whole' but omits the list's first member, 'Request/Execution attempt'; FX-13 repeats the same truncation as 'the full tuple file 03 names'
blockers.where: truthTables.tables[*].rows[*].GRANTED (one identical string, all 14 rows) and acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses.classes[13].intent (FX-13)
blockers.sourceAtBytes: docs/v2/architecture/03-configuration-and-security.md lines 105-106, at digest 52158469e805ca2c2e9a053282ac8428b9adf75184190c1cb6b4ebe2fce8425a: 'Broker grants bind Request/Execution attempt, component/generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, and expiry.'
blockers.artifactAtBytes: GRANTED: '...for a bound (component, generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, expiry) tuple -- file 03's binding list, carried whole --'. FX-13: 'every record binds the full tuple file 03 names (component/generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, expiry)'.
blockers.whatIMeasured: File 03's sentence names eight members, the first being 'Request/Execution attempt'. The artifact's tuple names eight items only because it splits the single member 'component/generation' into two; 'Request/Execution attempt' is absent from both the GRANTED column and FX-13. The artifact demonstrably knows the complete list: tensionsObserved T-4 quotes the whole sentence, 'Request/Execution attempt' included. So this is a truncation of a list the artifact holds correctly elsewhere, not a reading of a different source.
blockers.whyBlocking: Two independent grounds. (1) Restatement-authorship plus freeze 7.2.2: a block labelled 'carried whole' that omits a member of the list it carries is a recital that does not replicate at bytes, and it is replicated identically fourteen times in the column the DR-105 row names. (2) It has an effect-authority consequence rather than being a citation slip. Binding a grant to the Request/Execution attempt is what stops one durable grant record from being honoured across a second attempt within the same generation, operation and process instance. FX-13 is the only fixture class that would witness the binding, and it asserts the seven-member tuple as complete, so an implementation that never binds the attempt passes the artifact's own acceptance evidence and the DR-105 audit obligation is discharged against a tuple file 03 does not name.
blockers.repair: Restore 'Request/Execution attempt' to the GRANTED column tuple and to FX-13's assertion, or, if the authors hold that the attempt binds at the RA record rather than at the grant, say that explicitly and stop labelling the truncated tuple 'carried whole' / 'the full tuple file 03 names'. Note that this interacts with ID-DEP-P12: if the attempt identity is DR-006-parked, the ride must name it, since it is currently ridden silently.

blockers.title: ICO admits FAILED, but the irreversible boundary defines the disclosure for case (a) only as 'as completed', and FX-6 asserts that wording over every case-(a) effect -- mandating a false disclosure when a pre-revocation irreversible commit failed
blockers.whatIMeasured: L-5 states the outcome record 'Records COMPLETED, FAILED, or INDETERMINATE.' Across the whole artifact the string FAILED occurs exactly once -- in that sentence. INDETERMINATE occurs nine times and is given a complete, deterministic disclosure rule (indeterminateOutcome, FX-11). COMPLETED is given one (caseBefore, itMeans[3], FX-6). FAILED is given none. caseBefore covers case (a) by the ordering test alone -- 'n < r. The effect is recorded and disclosed as COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION' -- and itMeans[3] says the effect 'appears in the audit and in the operator-facing residual outcome, as completed'. R-3 repeats 'n < r: completed-before-revocation, disclosed, not undone'. FX-6 then forces the case and asserts over exact bytes 'that the effect is stated as completed'.
blockers.failureCase: An irreversible effect whose ICI is durable at n < r and whose ICO records FAILED. Case (a) applies by the ordering test, so caseBefore, itMeans[3] and FX-6 all apply, and all three say the operator-facing residual states the effect as completed. notRefusals[1] compounds this by classing COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION as an OUTCOME, alongside INDETERMINATE, rather than as a name for the ordering relation.
blockers.whyBlocking: The artifact's governing rule for this column is that disclosure is deterministic, derived from the record, and never softened or narrated away; FX-6 exists because 'the mechanics being right does not prevent the output from lying about them'. Here the mechanics are right -- ICO records FAILED -- and the artifact's own disclosure rule and its own wording golden instruct the output to lie about them. This is squarely inside the DR-105 row's 'reversible/irreversible effect-commit ... and audit' obligation, and it is a defect the artifact created rather than inherited: file 03 has no ICO vocabulary, so the FAILED value and its unstated disclosure are both this artifact's. An unspecified outcome-to-disclosure mapping on a defined path is not saved by the term-of-art reading, because itMeans[3] and FX-6 use the plain word 'completed' rather than the compound term.
blockers.repair: Define the (ICO = FAILED, n < r) disclosure explicitly and give it a name that is not 'completed' -- the honest content is that the commit was ordered before revocation and the effect did not land, that revocation did not reach it either, and that no undo is claimed. Rescope FX-6 to assert the wording appropriate to each ICO value rather than 'completed' for all of case (a). Consider whether COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION should be stated as a property of the ORDERING carried alongside the ICO value, rather than as an outcome value competing with it.

advisories.title: The actor model is SOUND on its own merits, but the artifact never resolves the actor for the one egress its slice actually exercises, and never states the host-actor ownership taxonomy in one place
advisories.judgedIndependently: I did not adopt the coherence review's framing. I read the DR-105 row and its source pin myself. File 03's 'Proposed permissions with honest outcomes' is component-and-broker text end to end: per-operation resolution into requested/granted/denied, 'a manifest, repository, or publisher cannot grant authority to itself', broker grants bound to component/generation and process instance, revocation invalidating 'later use by the component and every descendant', audit binding broker request IDs. Every obligation the row's acceptance-evidence cell names -- the five-column matrix, the linearization over acceptance and effect-commit, revocation, cleanup, audit -- is stated over grant generations and brokered requests. A host writing to a path the invoking user named on the command line has no requested record, no grant, no generation, and nothing revocation could reach; modelling it as a permission would require the user to be authorized against themselves. So the fourth deliberate non-token is correctly ruled, and a component-only permission model is the right shape for this row.
advisories.whatTheExclusionImplies: Host-actor authorization is owned elsewhere and the artifact names the owners case by case: DR-123's CLI baseline with DR-G17's serialization-failure behavior for user-named output paths; DR-114 for consented doctor probes and egress, whose file 04 text already carries the disclosure obligation ('Every consented action reports scope, endpoint/bytes where relevant, result, and residual limitation'); DR-124/DR-G19 for host state writes and for clock and entropy as undeclared Plan inputs. What follows from that, and is not said anywhere I could measure, is that NO row currently carries a per-platform enforced/disclosed matrix for host-originated effects. That is a coordinator routing question, not a defect in this artifact.
advisories.theGapThatIsThisArtifactsToClose: PT-NET-EGRESS is minted, and its sliceJustification says it 'exists in slice 1 in exactly one posture -- DENIED by default, and reachable only through DR-114's named doctor consent'. But file 04 at bytes says 'Doctor defaults to read-only, no component code, no network, and no mutation', and the named consent covers 'component/customer tool execution, probes, or egress' -- three things, of which probes and egress need not have a component actor. If a consented doctor probe is HOST-executed, then the slice's only exercised egress has no cell in this table at all, because REQUESTED is defined as 'A declaration in the admitted manifest' and a host probe has no manifest -- and PT-NET-EGRESS becomes a minted token with no slice-1 exerciser, which is precisely the condition the artifact used to keep fs.write.project RESERVED ('Minting a token no slice-1 surface exercises would put an unexercised grant path in the vocabulary'). tensionsObserved T-3 names the adjacent question -- whether the consent is a GRANT record or a DR-114 record -- but not the actor question, and ID-DEP-P3 rides DR-114 without naming it either.
advisories.repair: Add the actor question to T-3 and to ID-DEP-P3 explicitly: state that if the consented probe's egress is host-originated, PT-NET-EGRESS has no slice-1 exerciser and either withdraws to RESERVED on the same reasoning as fs.write.project or is restated as covering only a component-originated egress that slice 1 may not contain. State once, in one place, who owns host-actor authorization, so that the fourth non-token's ruling reads as a taxonomy rather than as a single carve-out.

advisories.title: The DISCLOSED column is one identical string across all 14 rows and elaborates only the DISCLOSURE-ONLY case, so the two enforcement states that carry their own disclosure obligations do not have them in the column that states obligations
advisories.whatIMeasured: REQUESTED, GRANTED, DENIED and DISCLOSED each have exactly one distinct value across all 14 rows. Uniformity is defensible for the three authorization columns, whose per-token variance genuinely lives in permissionVocabulary.tokens. It is not defensible for DISCLOSED, which columnSemantics defines as 'An OBLIGATION on the host's output and audit, DERIVED FROM THE ENFORCED VALUE' -- and the ENFORCED value varies.
advisories.whatIsMissingFromIt: enforcementStateVocabulary states that ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER 'carries a mandatory paired disclosure', and the two PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED cells carry it in outsideTheClaim -- but the DISCLOSED column does not. The two PT-ENV-READ cells state that the broad claim ('the component cannot learn a denied variable's value') is DISCLOSURE-ONLY and warn that 'a reader who needs the broad claim does not have it' -- but the DISCLOSED column does not oblige the host to say so. The column's only elaboration is 'On a DISCLOSURE-ONLY cell...'. On the four cells where an over-read into confinement is most likely, the column that exists to prevent that reading is generic.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The obligations do exist in the artifact, at the cells, and FX-2B, FX-5 and FX-8 are written to catch the over-read. This is a placement defect, not a missing obligation. But the artifact's own rule -- 'Silence is not disclosure' -- applies to its own table, and the DR-105 row names 'disclosed' as a column.
advisories.repair: Make DISCLOSED per-cell, derived as columnSemantics already says it is: on ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, carry the paired disclosure; on ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION, carry the narrowing so that the operator is told which claim is enforced and which residue is not.

advisories.title: AUD's terminality is unspecified, and the artifact's own text admits records after it -- an unspecified transition pair
advisories.whatIMeasured: Nothing states that AUDIT-SEALED is the last record of a generation or what the single writer does with a record that would order above it. Two of the artifact's own rules produce such records: R-5 says a later revocation attempt is 'Recorded as a duplicate revocation record with its own sequence number', and indeterminateOutcome says 'An INDETERMINATE that is later resolved by external means is a new record, never an edit.' Both can land after AUD. L-8's guarantee -- 'The audit binding is complete for the generation' -- then has no determinate meaning: it is either falsified by the later record, or the seal reopens, and the artifact does not say which.
advisories.scope: This is bookkeeping rather than effect authority; no ENFORCED value and no refusal depends on it. But the DR-105 row names audit, and the artifact's claim is that the order is total and every state's successors determinate.
advisories.repair: Add the rule: either AUD is terminal and a post-seal fact opens a new sealed segment (with its own AUD) that references the prior seal, or AUD is re-issued and the earlier seal is superseded by record rather than by edit. Extend FX-4's assertion set to cover a record ordering above AUD.

advisories.title: The linearization's single-writer and durability guarantees hold against crash and concurrency but not against a same-user component in the TCB, and the artifact never says so
advisories.whatIMeasured: The strings tamper, integrity, forge and rewrite occur zero times in the artifact. theOrder.carrier asserts 'ONE durable, append-only grant journal ... with exactly one writer: the host, holding the project/operation lock. There is no second ordering authority anywhere in this design.' On 24 of 28 cells the artifact's own finding is that the component is unconstrained trusted code in the TCB holding the invoking user's ambient authority, and FX-2B asserts affirmatively that its ambient writes succeed. Such a component can write the journal file. The single-writer property is therefore a host-side design invariant, not a property enforced against the actor the rest of the artifact is careful about.
advisories.whyNotABlocker: It falsifies no ENFORCED cell. The ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER claim is scoped to 'no effect is performed BY THE HOST, on the brokered route, that the grant did not authorize', and its mandatory paired disclosure already concedes the component may perform the effect directly with ambient authority -- so journal tampering buys the component nothing it did not already have, and is not an escalation. The artifact makes no tamper-resistance claim that this falsifies. The finding is an omission, in an artifact whose standard elsewhere is to state exactly this kind of residue.
advisories.repair: State it where the ambient residue is already stated: the ordering guarantees are against crash, concurrency and clock manipulation, not against a TCB member with write access to the journal bytes, and the audit is correspondingly bounded. FX-4 and FX-7 should be labelled as testing the former and not the latter, exactly as FX-3 is already labelled 'NOTHING WIDER'.

advisories.title: PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE's CONDITIONALLY-REVERSIBLE ruling sits under a rule forbidding per-request reversibility, and the RCI-versus-ICI successor for it is derivable but not stated
advisories.whatIMeasured: effectCommitDefinitions.rule: 'Reversibility is a declared property of an EFFECT CLASS, never inferred per request and never asserted by a component.' byToken then makes PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE 'CONDITIONALLY REVERSIBLE, and only for a HOST-STAGED write in which the host retained the prior bytes until CLN', with a direct component write irreversible to the host.
advisories.resolution: The two are reconcilable and I did reconcile them: only host-staged writes travel the brokered route, so only they get RCI/ICI records at all, and a direct component write is unrecorded ambient activity with no journal presence. The successor is therefore determinate. But the artifact does not say this, and a reader walking the state machine sees one token whose commit-intent type appears to depend on how a particular write was performed -- which the governing rule says never happens.
advisories.repair: State that the brokered route for this token is host-staged by construction, so the class property is uniform on every record that exists, and that the 'direct component write' half of the ruling describes the ambient path which produces no record.

advisories.title: Grant-generation rollover is not among the ten races and is not named as out of scope
advisories.whatIMeasured: theOrder.whyOneJournalAndNotPerGrant asserts 'Comparing two grants in different generations is not defined and is not needed -- no rule in this contract compares across generations.' No race walks a request or an unfinished cleanup that spans a generation boundary. The register cell names already-accepted requests, in-flight requests and irreversible effects, and R-1, R-2 and R-3 cover those three, so the cell's named race set is discharged; rollover is not among the cell's named races.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Generation semantics are DR-107's ('Project/operation lock and multi-version generation semantics'), which the artifact already rides at ID-DEP-P6. Ownership exists; the omission is that the race list does not say the rollover case is ridden rather than decided.
advisories.repair: Either add the case as an eleventh race resolved by the per-generation journal boundary, or name it in whatThisDoesNotDo as ridden on DR-107.

whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.censusAndDecomposition: Recounted mechanically. 2 platforms (macos, linux, no duplicates) x 7 tokens (identical order to permissionVocabulary.tokens, no duplicates, no omissions) x 2 execution modes (child-process, in-host-process on every row) = 28 cells, with no combination missing and none duplicated. byState and byPlatformAndMode replicate exactly. Every one of the 28 cells carries all five required fields (enforced, mechanism, scopeOfClaim, outsideTheClaim, futurePrimitiveDetermination) as non-empty strings. The derived recital 'OPEN on 12 of the 14 child-process cells' replicates: 12 of 14 carry futurePrimitiveDetermination beginning OPEN, the two exceptions being the PT-ENV-READ cells. All declared collection counts replicate: 7 tokens, 4 deliberate non-tokens, 6 reserved/excluded extension points, 8 transitions L-1..L-8, 10 races R-1..R-10, 9 refusal families PR-1..PR-9, 14 fixture classes (FX-1, FX-2A, FX-2B, FX-3..FX-13), 13 identity dependencies ID-DEP-P1..P13, 5 tensions T-1..T-5, 12 whatThisDoesNotDo entries, 7 coverageObligation mapping members.
whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.enforcementHonesty: This is the centre of gravity and it holds. Of 28 cells, 24 are DISCLOSURE-ONLY with mechanism 'None' and an explicit statement that the component is trusted code in the TCB for that effect class -- which is the honest answer for D-002's first-party, no-sandbox slice and is what file 02's TCB sentence and file 03's confinement-honesty section require. I attacked the four enforced cells directly. (1) PT-ENV-READ / ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION, child-process, both platforms: the named mechanism is the envp argument to execve(2) and the environment array passed to posix_spawn(3). Both exist on macOS and on Linux; no platform-specific confinement facility is claimed. The claim is scoped to 'a variable not granted is absent from the child process's OWN environment block ... the contents of one array at one moment of process creation', and a same-user process cannot make the host place a variable in an array the host builds. I looked for the escape and the artifact has already closed it in the honest direction: outsideTheClaim states that the broad claim -- that the component cannot LEARN a denied variable's value -- is DISCLOSURE-ONLY, that same-user introspection paths exist on general-purpose operating systems, and that this session measured none of them. whatThisDoesNotDo[10] repeats it, honestyRatio carries the narrowing ('scoped to the child's own environment block') rather than flattening it, and FX-3 is explicitly bounded to the narrow claim and 'NOTHING WIDER'. This is an enforced value that is true as scoped, with the residue disclosed at every place the value is summarised. (2) PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED / ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, child-process, both platforms: scoped to 'no effect is performed BY THE HOST, on the brokered route, that the grant did not authorize', with file 03's own sentence carried as the paired disclosure -- 'Host brokers used voluntarily by an unconstrained same-user process do not create confinement' -- and the explicit statement that the component may perform the same effect directly and the host will neither observe nor record it. That is the corpus's required shape rather than a bypass of it. I tested the obvious alternate path, a same-user component writing the grant journal directly: it does not falsify this cell, because the cell already concedes the component can perform the effect without the host, so subverting the grant is not an escalation (recorded separately as A-4 because the artifact never states it). Zero cells claim enforcement by a primitive that does not exist; zero cells nominate a confinement primitive at all, which the artifact states deliberately and which I confirmed by reading every futurePrimitiveDetermination field.
whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.inHostProcessMode: All 14 in-host-process cells are DISCLOSURE-ONLY with the mechanism 'None, in this mode, for any token', reasoned from shared address space and the absence of a second envp. The prototype's own guard module is quoted against itself here rather than carried forward as a mechanism, and whatThisDoesNotDo[9] refuses to endorse those guards. The two-mode split is stated as gated on ID-DEP-P10 with the consequence named plainly: 'the single determination that decides whether FOUR cells in this table are enforced or ZERO are'.
whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.nonTokensAndReservedPoints: The four deliberate non-tokens are each ruled with a reason and an owner, and each is inside D-002's slice scoping. Clock and entropy are routed to DR-124/DR-G19 as determinism concerns rather than authority concerns, which matches file 04's undeclared-Plan-inputs negative-test sentence at bytes. Host output is ruled out against file 02's existing prohibition on components choosing UI, verdicts or exits. The fourth is treated at A-1. The six reserved/excluded points each name a minting owner: fs.write.project (no slice-1 surface mutates project files; verified against file 04's doctor sentence and D-002's analyze-only slice), secret-handle (DR-108 deferred by D-002), artifact broker (authoritative evidence custody excluded wholly from slice 1), argument-vector scoping (DR-125 or a successor), inbound/listening/IPC/device (no measured source names one; the prototype's coarse class set carries none either, which I confirmed at resource-requirement.ts), and third-party execution (EXCLUDED per the DR-105 row's own consequence column, verified at the register). I found no excluded surface that carries effect authority the slice needs, with the single exception raised at A-1.
whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.linearizationDeterminism: I walked the eight transitions as a state machine. The order is TOTAL by construction: one journal per (project, grant generation), one writer holding the project/operation lock, strictly increasing unsigned sequence numbers derived from the journal's own last durable value. It is DURABLE across crash: a record is ordered only when its bytes are durable, an in-memory sequence assignment 'orders NOTHING and gates NOTHING', recovery replays and resumes at last-durable-plus-one, and numbers are never reused, reordered or renumbered by migration. Every one of L-1..L-8 has an afterCrash rule and I found no crash point with ambiguous recovery: RA with no successor is CANCELED-BY-RECOVERY, safe without observing the world because no effect can precede its own commit-intent; RCI with no outcome runs the class's idempotent inverse; ICI with no outcome is the hard case and gets ICO = INDETERMINATE with an explicit refusal to guess, retry, assume failure or assume success -- and the artifact names why 'assume failed then retry' is the most dangerous of the three, which is correct; RCO and ICO are terminal and recovery never re-derives or upgrades them; CLN re-runs safely on declared idempotence; an unsealed generation is disclosed unsealed rather than sealed retroactively. The irreversible boundary is stated as a comparison of two integers with exactly two cases and n = r impossible, and case (b) -- r < n -- is closed by construction rather than handled: after REV is durable the single writer refuses to write an ICI for the generation, so the forbidden state is unreachable rather than merely undesirable, which is file 03's 'An irreversible effect not yet committed at the point is forbidden' given a mechanism. I probed reviewGuidance's own challenge on case (b) and found no path by which an ICI orders above r, because initiation strictly follows durable intent and there is no second writer. What revocation MEANS after an irreversible commit is stated deterministically as four things and explicitly not as seven others -- 'not undone, reversed, rolled back, compensated, neutralized, contained, or mitigated' -- with compensation ruled a NEW effect needing its own authorization and its own records, and with orderingIsOverRecordsNotWorldEvents bounding every before/after to the journal. The only gap I found in this section is B-3.
whatIVerifiedAndFoundSound.raceSemantics: All ten outcomes are derived from sequence-number comparisons in the one journal rather than asserted independently, and I found no inconsistency between any race and the linearization. The register cell's three named race classes are all covered: already-accepted requests (R-1), in-flight requests (R-2, which correctly refuses to treat 'in flight' as a third state), and irreversible effects (R-3, which defers wholly to the boundary rule rather than restating it differently). R-4's exclusivity tie-break is by lower sequence with no queueing or promotion; R-5 separates state-level idempotence from record-level non-idempotence cleanly; R-7 carries file 03's own denial sentence; R-8 is the strongest row in the artifact, asserting the brokered refusal AND the ambient success and requiring FX-8 to run both halves so the evidence cannot be read as confinement; R-9 makes scope changes ordinary journal records with no separate configuration-reload path; R-10 materialises expiry as a record so that the clock is never the order, which obeys DR-G09's waiver-rule cell verbatim. I hunted for unenumerated races. Scope WIDENING, expiry racing revocation, crash between REV and cleanup, and a second REV during cleanup are all derivable from the stated rules. Two candidates were not derivable and are recorded as A-3 (post-AUD records) and A-7 (generation rollover); neither is in the register cell's named set.
